end.summary:
Sequenced the Company’s rise from the 1600 charter through Plassey (1757), Buxar (1764), Diwani, and Crown rule (1858); practised, with a why or new-situation check still needed.
Practised how alliances, battles, Diwani revenue, and armies increased Company control; explanations were partly right and still need checking across examples.
Practised colonial economic effects using textiles, raw cotton, revenue demands, debt, and indigo; explanations were partly right and still need checking.
Practised Indian resistance through the 1857 revolt and Champaran; easy questions were answered, with a why or new-situation check still needed.
Practised comparing an official view with Dadabhai Naoroji’s drain-of-wealth view; source comparison is still partly right and needs further checking.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the Company’s timeline, Plassey and Buxar, revenue collection, textile changes, farmer debt, indigo, resistance, and contrasting historical sources. Zoya used useful cause-and-effect links, such as Diwani revenue supporting trade and armies, and compared an officer’s account with Dadabhai Naoroji’s view. Some explanations still need checking with a new situation, especially the methods of gaining power, economic effects, and source evidence; no later correction of these points was recorded. At home, ask Zoya to explain one event using “what happened, why it helped the Company, and what changed afterward.”
